strengths: The paper identifies a useful distinction between explaining predictions through raw inputs and through interpretable macro-level features. Its discussion of confounding induced by omitted macro-level variables offers an identifiable contribution for researchers in explainability and causal discovery.

Using PAGs and FCI is a principled way to represent uncertainty about latent confounding. The background constraint that predictions cannot cause image content is well motivated, and the approach fits the proposed setting without access to model internals.

The explicit synthetic data-generating process, two annotated-image applications, bootstrap analyses, and alternative discovery algorithm make the proposal concrete. The writing generally explains the causal framework clearly and acknowledges important limitations involving faithfulness, annotation errors, and partial identification.
weaknesses: Necessary: Correct the interpretation of the graph summaries in Sections 6.3–6.4 and Figures 9–10. Pooling directed and partially directed edges does not establish causation: a partially directed edge can remain compatible with pure confounding, even when selected consistently. Conversely, absence of an edge adjacent to the prediction does not exclude an indirect causal effect. Figure 10 itself contains Cardiomegaly o→ Atelectasis → prediction, illustrating a possible causal pathway missed by the adjacency ranking. Report definite and possible ancestry separately and revise claims that low-ranked features are not causally relevant.

Necessary: Repair the Shapley counterexample in Section 3.3 and Appendix A. Appendix A.2 declares Z3 unobserved but retains its fixed value in the coalition payoffs; this does not derive an observable estimator performing adjustment using only Z2. Appendix A.1 also uses marginal replacements that do not propagate interventions through the stated Z2,Z3 → Z1 relationships, so its interpretation as the correct causal calculation is unsupported. Define the intervention game and the estimator precisely, then rederive the comparison or remove this example. The general concern about confounding remains valid independently.

Necessary: Address selection in the pneumonia experiment. Section 6.1 compares 120 pneumonia images with 120 controls explicitly selected for having no findings. This selection depends on disease status and the explanatory findings, potentially inducing dependencies beyond those represented by the assumed model without selection bias. The manuscript needs a justified treatment of this sampling mechanism, an appropriate alternative sample, or substantially narrower interpretation of the resulting graph.

Necessary: Establish the reliability of the conditional-independence tests used in the applications. The bird analysis uses multivalued attributes and conditioning sets of up to four variables, while the X-ray analysis has only 240 images and potentially rare findings. These settings raise substantial sparse-contingency-table concerns for asymptotic chi-square tests. Report the actual discovery sample sizes and relevant count diagnostics, and use suitably calibrated tests where needed. Bootstrap edge frequencies alone do not resolve systematic testing errors.

Necessary: Narrow the empirical causal conclusions or supply stronger validation. Clinical or ornithological plausibility does not distinguish causal features from correlated proxies. Moreover, the bird sensitivity analysis changes the leading findings substantially: Wing Shape and Tail Shape rank highly under FCI but much lower under GRaSP-FCI, while Crown Color moves from near the bottom to the top. The explicit simulation supports an illustrative example, but the real-data results currently support exploratory hypotheses more convincingly than validated causal explanations.

Optional: Comparisons using the same macro-level annotations would better isolate the benefit of causal discovery from the benefit of supplying interpretable features. The LIME/SHAP examples mainly illustrate differences in representation and explanation scope. Releasing an executable pipeline with exact splits and configurations would also improve reproducibility.
